what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat Parkinson's disease. It helps reduce symptoms like shaking (tremors), stiffness, and slow movement. Levodopa is converted into dopamine in your brain, which helps control movement. Carbidopa helps levodopa work better and reduces side effects like nausea.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You may take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. If it upsets your stomach, taking it with a small snack may help. Do NOT crush, chew, or break extended-release tablets (Sinemet CR or Rytary) — swallow them whole. For regular (immediate-release) tablets, your doctor may tell you to split them if needed. Try to take each dose at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep your symptoms under control.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find what works best for you. Everyone's dose is different. A common starting dose for adults is one tablet of carbidopa 25 mg / levodopa 100 mg taken three times a day. Do not change your dose on your own. It may take weeks for your doctor to adjust your dose to the right amount.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. Missing doses can cause your Parkinson's symptoms to return or worsen, so try your best to take this medicine on schedule.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in a tightly closed container. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating high-protein meals (like large amounts of meat, cheese, or eggs) right before or after taking your dose, as protein can reduce how well levodopa works. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause sudden sleepiness or dizziness. Avoid getting up too quickly from sitting or lying down to prevent dizziness or falls. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: uncontrolled or unusual movements of your face, arms, or legs (called dyskinesia); sudden urge to sleep without warning during the day; feeling confused, seeing or hearing things that are not there (hallucinations); unusual changes in mood or behavior; signs of depression or thoughts of self-harm; compulsive behaviors such as gambling, eating, or sexual urges that are new or hard to control; dark or bloody urine; or fever with muscle stiffness. Also call your doctor if your Parkinson's symptoms suddenly get much worse or if you have trouble swallowing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your movement and symptoms within a few days to a few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several weeks or even months for your doctor to adjust the dose to the best level for you. This medicine controls symptoms but does not cure Parkinson's disease. Keep taking it even if you feel better.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, confusion, and hallucinations. Use caution when standing up to avoid falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully known. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how your body processes the medicine. Children: This medicine is generally not used in patients under 18 years old.
